title: `abortRef` is write-only — assigned but never read
description: The hook declares `const abortRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null)` (line 15) and assigns it inside the mount effect (`abortRef.current = controller`, line 39), but the ref is never read anywhere. The effect's cleanup aborts the *local* `controller` variable (`return () => { controller.abort() }`), not `abortRef.current`. The manual `fetchForPath` call path never consults `abortRef` either. The ref therefore serves no purpose and gives the misleading impression that in-flight requests are tracked/cancellable across calls when they are not.
evidence: Line 15 declares ref; line 38 creates `const controller = new AbortController()`; line 39 `abortRef.current = controller`; line 42 calls `fetchForPath(initialPath, controller.signal)`; cleanup (line 44-46) calls `controller.abort()` using the closure variable, not `abortRef.current`. Grep for `abortRef` in the file returns only the declaration (15) and the assignment (39) — zero reads.
est_reduction: 2 lines (the ref declaration + the assignment), plus removes a false signal that request cancellation is centrally tracked.
behavior_preservation: Removing the unused ref does not change any observable behavior: cleanup already aborts via the local `controller`, and no code reads `abortRef.current`.
